items.title: Is Comcast Broken, Or Just Paying To Defend Its Broadband?
items.summary: Comcast (CMCSA) shares sit about 43% below their two-year high, a price that looks like a bet the business is shrinking. Yet over the past twelve months Comcast generated nearly $18 billion of free cash flow, a yield of 22.2% on its market value against 4.5% for the median S&P 500 company. Which reading is right? It turns on a choice Comcast made more than a year ago: lower broadband prices to hold customers against new rivals.

items.title: Charter Communications (CHTR) Eyes Cable Deals With CFO Pushing A Disciplined Approach
items.summary: Charter Communications (NasdaqGS:CHTR) is evaluating potential cable sector acquisitions as part of its current corporate agenda. The firm's CFO has highlighted a disciplined merger framework that prioritises financial prudence and balance sheet resilience. Management has indicated that any transaction would need to align with existing capital allocation plans and leverage targets. items.title: Is Verizon Stock Cheap, Or Just Done Growing?
items.summary: Verizon Communications (VZ) trades at about 12 times earnings, against an S&P 500 median of 22.4. A discount that wide usually follows a collapse. Not here. The stock returned 14.1% over the past twelve months, behind the index's 17.9%, and management has raised parts of its 2026 guidance in two straight quarters. So is this a good business on sale or a fair price for a company that has stopped growing.

items.title: How Far Can Comcast Stock Fall, And How Long Would You Wait?
items.summary: Comcast (CMCSA) trades near $22, about 29% below its 52-week high, and the market has not been falling with it. The S&P 500 returned close to 18% over the past year, while Comcast lost about 21%. The company is in the middle of a broadband pivot that it says is holding its own results down. So the question is not how hard Comcast drops in a crisis. It is how long it stays down.

items.title: Why Does AT&T Stock Cost Less Than A Slower-Growing Verizon?
items.summary: AT&T (T) grows faster than Verizon, yet it trades at a far lower multiple of earnings. In its five-company peer group it ranks second on growth and margin but only third on its earnings multiple. Management calls that a disparity, and it has raised its buyback to take advantage of it.

items.summary: Spectrum is confronting a new challenge as rivals continue to put pressure on its internet business.

items.title: Is Verizon Stock Cheap, Or Is Its Cash Already Spoken For?
items.summary: Verizon Communications (VZ) trades near $48 a share and generated free cash worth 10.0% of its market value over the last twelve months. The median S&P 500 company manages 4.5%. A gap that wide usually means one of two things: a bargain, or a business the market expects to shrink. Verizon is neither, quite. The cash is real, and it is not all yours.
